explanation: The woodblock print, made around 1831, belongs to Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Thousands of impressions were printed from the carved blocks and sold cheaply.

claims.text: Mount Fuji appears small in the background of The Great Wave off Kanagawa.
The Great Wave off Kanagawa does not show a rising sun, a pagoda or a lighthouse.
Hokusai's The Great Wave off Kanagawa is a woodblock print made around 1831, part of the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
Thousands of impressions of The Great Wave were printed from woodblocks and sold cheaply.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The British Museum says as many as 8,000 impressions of each design were printed, and several hundred of these still exist today. Other sources give lower figures. One Seattle Art Museum page puts the original run at about 3,000 impressions during Hokusai's lifetime. ... the British Museum notes that one cost little more than a double helping of noodles in Edo.

claimResults.note: Estimates run from about 3,000 to 8,000 and no records survive, so 'thousands' is the safe form; do not tighten it. British Museum and Seattle Art Museum are museums holding impressions.
